A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching methods, experiments, and appendices A–H. Their text, equations, and figures are readable and support comparison, including the expanded appendices in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original RoBERTa experiments on construction distinctions, idiomatic expressions, and schematic constructions, including classification results and affinity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on NPNs absent from Pile-train and analyses of individual idioms.

M1.justification: Both versions use RoBERTa-large masked-word probabilities for global affinity and Jensen–Shannon divergence under additional masking for local affinity. V2 changes the matrix index convention and clarifies diagonal averaging in Appendix B.4; these do not establish a different underlying method.

E1.justification: The existing English construction datasets and tasks remain. V2 adds a focused NPN test scenario using nouns whose NPN combinations have zero occurrences in Pile-train: 91 retained nouns generate 364 sentences (Section 6.1 and Appendix E.4). This extends coverage to an explicitly frequency-controlled population.

E2.justification: The comparisons with Zhou et al.'s GPT, Llama, and Llama-adjective probes remain, with unchanged quoted accuracies. Both versions explicitly avoid reimplementing those comparisons. Newly cited perturbed-masking methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds an explicit prior-attestation control through Pile-based rejection sampling and per-idiom comparisons requiring at least five sentences of each usage type. It also revises the retained random-NPN evaluation: v1 reports 295 valid generations and 162 acceptable sentences, while v2 describes 400 generations, eight omissions, and 244 acceptable sentences. These substantially extend the evaluation design and change the analyzed sample.

E4.justification: V2 adds a controlled NPN generalization test with acceptable-only and unfiltered analyses, plus extensive MAGPIE diagnostics examining individual idioms, contextual differences, and labeling errors. Appendix B.4 also revises the EAP/AAP sensitivity and error analysis. These go beyond the earlier pooled idiom result and random-NPN analysis.

E5.justification: UMAP seed-sensitivity reporting expands from two displayed seed columns in v1 Figure 12 to three in v2 Figure 14. However, v2 Appendix B.4 still says two columns, leaving inconsistent run-count documentation. Neither version adds confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the random-NPN affinity distributions under the revised sample, adds zero-frequency challenge results and per-idiom scores, and revises EAP/AAP salient interactions and flagged examples. For example, the new MAGPIE analysis reports join the club at 0.20 figurative versus 0.49 literal affinity. The headline CEC result of 272/277 and MAGPIE AUC of 0.71 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The underlying affinity definitions and mathematical discussion of matrix asymmetry and diagonal values are retained. Swapping the local-affinity indices aligns notation with the existing row/column convention; no substantive derivation, formal assumption, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claim that distributions reveal constructional information but affinity alone is insufficient for complete construction induction. The introduction narrows the methodological contribution from developing intervention methods to extending prior perturbed-masking work.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 becomes more cautious about EAP/AAP separation, replacing the asserted discovery of three mislabeled examples with imperfect separation and discussion of likely classification errors. V2 also explains idiom failures through entrenchment, context length, and syntactic variation, and explicitly acknowledges English-only coverage. The principal limitations of affinity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies UMAP n_neighbors=10 and min_dist=0.1, detailed CoGS counts, MAGPIE confidence/offset/token filtering, and the NPN frequency-screening procedure. These improve documentation without establishing that every newly described filter was newly introduced. Some MAGPIE sentence totals in Appendix D.2 do not reconcile; model, hardware, generation settings, and code/data access remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions the method as an extension of perturbed masking, citing Wu et al. (2020) and Hoover et al. (2021), where v1 primarily emphasized collostructional analysis and intervention methods. It also substantially expands the idiom and causal-method literature. This changes the attribution and positioning of the methodological contribution, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introductory motivation, refines substantive/schematic section headings, moves CoGS examples from Appendix C into Section 5.1, and reorganizes the NPN supplement. It also edits wording, affiliations, and acknowledgements. The overall sequence of nine main sections and appendices A–H is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the opening method schematic, an annotated UMAP plot, two NPN challenge plots, and the two-page per-idiom Figure 22. It redraws the EAP/AAP difference heatmap with directional colors and expands the UMAP grid to three columns. Together these substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the generalization evidence with a concrete frequency control, makes idiom failures and uncertain EAP/AAP separation more transparent, and improves attribution to prior methods. These are useful gains over v1's evidence and framing. Their scope remains limited: Pile-train is only a proxy for RoBERTa's training data, and inconsistent appendix sample totals and seed descriptions reduce the benefits of the added documentation.
